questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me the most important was to get the opportunity to study Chinese and practice on a daily basis.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The randomness of the course selection system created a lot of problems for me.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult, I kept calling concerning course selection problems and could not get assistance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of assistance concerning covid rules and procedures.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was not sufficient information and guidance concerning course selections and the selection system.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A dormitory that was located outside campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No real options for meal plans - there was a very limited kitchen on the ground floor but I stayed on the 12th floor and it can take up to five minutes to get down.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of mould, the bathroom was full of mould and even though I dried my clothing outside on the balcony I had to throw out two shirts because of the mold. Also, do not use the dry clean facility! I did it and the facility that works with the dormitory destroyed a lot of my clothing. The don't mind putting needles through silk clothing etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The staff was helpful but the building was in a bad condition, dirty and the rooms for two people were extremely small.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid the process was complicated and I lost a couple of classes because one course that I was registered to attend through the online system was not properly registered and I did not get the class links when the course started and it took weeks before I was informed on the class material.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did not have enough courses but could only register through emailing the professors and they did not answer.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No help for registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful. The professors did not answer and I had to register for classes where it was not necessary to email professors in the last minute but these classes were not related to my studies and even though the course description said that no prerequisites were required to attend the course that was not true at all and the courses were quite demanding. Because I was registered late I missed the deadline to cancel the courses and was force to attend and fail one course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to register for at least five times the amount of courses that you need from the beginning. If not, you will not be accepted to enough courses and will end up having to find courses during a casino like period where you can almost only add courses through contacting professors that don't answer (with few exceptions) and in the end will end up chosing those that do not require this option which are mostly science courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good classes but each course had a workload that does not correspond to the workload of the same amount of points in Copenhagen. One course required an attendance of 4 hours each week with 2-4 hours of homework, 2 oral presentations that required 6 hours of preparation and 3 exams throughout the semester that consisted of both an oral and written exam. This course only gave 2 Danish ECTS.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels of the courses were fine but the workload big.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Every course was different according to the style of the professors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Enhancing Chinese language, General Chinese language, Chinese historical stories, Ancient Greek Literature, English Romanticism, The organisms that changed History, Introduction to Marine Geology and the course that I did go to exam in: introduction to neurology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Chinese Historical stories for those who want to improve their Chinese.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay your electricity, you have to but your own mattress and pillow

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were not so informed about the options probably due to covid

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Introduction to calligraphy, Chinese painting, mahjong, baking food - on an introductory level for an evening of fun. There were clubs, but I mostly got invitations to a Buddhist club that wanted to recruit people to Buddhism and becoming vegetarian.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally, I invested time in outside campus activities such as martial arts and archery. The campus had taekwondo but I am more interested in kungfu.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: National museum of art, the temples, Sun Moon Lake, Hualien, the south.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are kind but many don't appreciate when you speak loudly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the cultural activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some Taiwanese speak with extremely low tone and it can be hard to practice Chinese in those cases.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and calmness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Register for a lot of courses beforehand, don't bring nice quality clothing because the humidity can destroy it and the cleaners don't know how to treat it. Bring an empty suit case because you will find a lot of souvenirs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have a very good umbrella bring it, it rains a lot.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know the culture and Chinese language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The dialect.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The streets are not safe, I sprained a foot badly by stepping down into a hole next to the dormitory. Also, the scooter drivers are dangerous.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
